title: Nested-entity boundary guards and retry surface for streaming structured output
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When models stream structured payloads that contain nested objects/arrays and in-band tool/function call markers, transient truncation or mid-token chopping causes ambiguous boundaries that break downstream parsers or cause duplicate tool invocations. We also see incompatibilities across SDK versions that expect slightly different framing or escape interpretations. The ticket will design and implement defensive boundary guards and a clearly documented retry surface to make partial-stream recovery deterministic and safe for tool calls and for nested entities.

Goals:
- Define an in-stream 'entity boundary' sentinel semantics that can be emitted by the runtime when a chunk boundary splits a JSON token or nested entity (arrays, objects, strings containing escaped sequences).
- Ensure tool/function-call invocations are idempotent at the API surface when retries are attempted after a suspected truncation. Provide an idempotency token and a deterministic reconciliation protocol (accept, dedupe, or re-run) documented for SDKs.
- Normalize escape handling: adopt a canonical escape normalization step at the runtime edge so that clients receive a single unambiguous interpretation (e.g., convert mixed "\u000A" vs literal newlines to canonical form).
- Provide a small on-wire manifest and resume token that allows SDKs to request continuation from the server without re-executing previously-confirmed tool calls.
- Maintain backwards compatibility with older SDKs that cannot handle the new sentinel bytes: provide graceful degradation (fallback to existing best-effort reassembly heuristics).

Proposed approach:
1) Runtime emits a lightweight boundary marker (0x1E or JSON-safe marker string) when it detects that the next token or nested entity will be split across chunks. The marker includes a short resume token (base64) representing the KV-cache state and the current generation id.
2) The client SDK will interpret the marker: if it has previously acknowledged the preceding tool invocation, the SDK will request a continuation; otherwise the SDK will surface a retry action to the application layer with an idempotency token.
3) Tool/call safety: add an "invocation_state" header field returned with tool-call results; for retried streams the runtime will return a deterministic decision: "confirmed", "duplicate", or "unknown". SDKs map these to no-op, dedupe, or request re-run paths.
4) Escape canonicalization: introduce a canonicalize_escape passthrough before tokenization in the runtime so streamed strings are emitted with consistent escape sequences. Record this in the model profile so routing/fallbacks understand the normalization.
5) Fallbacks: if an SDK does not recognize the marker, the runtime will also emit a short textual hint in the last complete chunk that triggers older heuristics (non-breaking, human-readable).

Constraints and trade-offs:
- Extra bytes in the stream increase payload size slightly; we must quantify cost impact vs. benefit.
- The resume token leaks minimal internal state; ensure it contains no PII and is opaque (base64 of signed tuple).
- Idempotency increases complexity for server-side tool state; for now we scope to stateless functions and tool-call gates that can be replayed safely or deduped via invocation_state.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for nested entity split cases (strings with escaped quotes, arrays split across chunks, nested objects) pass with both new SDK and emulated legacy SDK behavior.
- Integration test where a streaming response contains a tool call that is split mid-invocation; outcome must be deterministic (no double tool execution) in 95% of runs and safe-fail otherwise with clear diagnostics.
- Update SDKs (python/js) to honor marker and resume token; publish compatibility doc and migration notes.
- Add observability metrics: "boundary_markers_emitted", "resume_requests", "invocations_deduped", and track P99 latency delta when markers are enabled.

Rollout plan:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag and controlled by per-customer config. Start with internal Canary customers and Redwood-internal workloads for two weeks. Then enable for a small percent of hosted traffic. Roll forward after metrics look stable.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests cover nested-object/array/string-split scenarios and pass in CI
SDKs (python/js) can resume without re-triggering confirmed tool invocations
Documentation published in Console and SDK changelogs explaining marker semantics and migration steps
Metrics emitted and no regression >5% in P99 latency for canary customers
comments: 2026-03-10: Initial write-up and scope alignment with PM (Jia Chen). Suggested focusing on tool-call idempotency first.
2026-03-11: Design review — agreed on using an opaque resume token + invocation_state header. @Liam O'Connor requested a smaller token size (<=64 bytes).
2026-03-11: @Design (Nina Rivera) reviewed UX for SDK errors — prefer deterministic error classes over opaque messages so apps can auto-retry.

2026-03-12: Spike results: prototype emitted marker using 0x1E and resume tokens ~48 bytes; reassembly test reduced ambiguous parses from 7% -> 0.5% on sampled demos. Link to spike notebook: https://drive.redwood.ai/spikes/stream-boundary-62789

2026-03-12: Created PR for runtime changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2487 — preliminary code for marker emission and canonicalize_escape hook. Pending unit tests and perf baseline.
2026-03-12: Security review queued; noted that resume token is signed and contains no customer data. Ticket for HSM signing assigned to ENG-63012.
